transcript:
Meeting header: 2028-04-11 15:00 UTC | Duration 48m | Attendees: Leah, Carlos (Redwood); Marta, Owen, Priya, Tommy (Ravenwood)

Summary: quick intros, high-level product fit, then ops/security deep dive.

00:00:05 Leah: Hey everyone thanks for carving out time, I'm Leah from Redwood Inference, i'm the AE on the account. happy to kick off.
00:00:12 Marta: Hi Leah, Marta here - head of platform at Ravenwood. we've been doing a lot of evaluation across providers, mostly focused on where data and logs end up.
00:00:22 Carlos: hi all, carlos, solutions eng. i'll handle the technicals and do the follow up bench plan.
00:00:28 Owen: Owen, security architect. quick note - we have regulatory constraints for investor PII and trade metadata, also looking at gdpr for our eu customers.
00:00:36 Tommy: Tommy, SRE. operationally we need deterministic retention windows and ability to purge.
00:00:41 Leah: Great. quick agenda - run through hosting options, keystore/residency, log flow and retention, evidence for audits, then next steps. sound good?
00:00:50 Priya: yep, legal perspective mainly about retention and legal-hold processes.

00:01:20 Carlos: so high level - Redwood offers Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC or on-prem). Hosted is fastest but logs and some telemetry live in Redwood cloud regions; we provide controls and logging endpoints and retention settings. Dedicated gives isolated capacity and stronger tenancy boundaries; Private gives you a private control plane and can be deployed into your VPC or on-prem for full network isolation.
00:02:03 Marta: couple of clarifying q's - with hosted, can we get region-locking so logs never leave eu-west-1? and what's the granularity of audit logs?
00:02:15 Carlos: yes region-locking is available as an option for hosted in our EU region; it's not absolute if you use multi-region fallbacks but we can configure policy to prefer eu-only and failover to dedicated variants. audit logs are delivered to a syslog/s3 endpoint you control or to our managed retention bucket; you can get raw request/response traces (redacted) and platform events.
00:02:45 Owen: when you say "redacted" - what fields are redacted? we need to ensure PII and trade identifiers are never stored in raw logs.
00:02:54 Carlos: default redaction removes obvious PII patterns and you can enable request-level masking; for strict cases we recommend private deployment so you can enforce no-logging at the control plane and run local parsers. there's also tokenization hooks at the client side.
00:03:16 Marta: okay, what about KMS? our compliance wants keys to be resident in eu with customer-managed keys and ability to rotate and escrow.
00:03:26 Carlos: Private supports your KMS via customer-managed KMS/HSM integration. Dedicated supports bring-your-own-key for model encryption, and Hosted supports CMKs with key residency in EU (subject to contract addendum). we do not currently offer key escrow by default, but we can discuss escrow arrangements for enterprise private deals.
00:03:54 Priya: legal-hold - if a regulator issues a hold, how quickly can logs be frozen and handed to us? and what's the chain of custody?
00:04:02 Leah: good question. our playbook for dedicated/private is documented - we can freeze snapshots within your environment (private) or from dedicated pools within SLA windows, we maintain tamper-evident audit trails and supply hashes and signed manifests for exports. for hosted we provide export timelines and notifications; exact SLA depends on the support tier and contract.
00:04:28 Owen: do you have SOC 2/ISO attestation artifacts available for review?
00:04:33 Leah: yes SOC 2 Type II reports, ISO 27001 certs, and penetration test summaries - i'll attach sanitized artifacts to the follow up.
00:04:42 Tommy: our ops question - we run automated PII redaction in upstream services. we want to avoid sending verbatim PII to any third party; can Redwood accept client-side redacted payloads and still provide embeddings/semantic search?
00:04:55 Carlos: absolutely, client-side redaction and deterministic tokenization is supported; for embeddings you can provide hashed tokens and we can match hashes if you bring the same hashing scheme. there's caveats with quality so we'll demo tradeoffs in the bench.
00:05:22 Marta: also about logs — retention windows. we need retention for 7 years for certain audit records, but short retention for derivatives. can you configure per-stream retention?
00:05:35 Carlos: yes per-stream retention config exists on Dedicated and Private; Hosted has tiered retention policies with longer-term archival options. we can set different TTLs for request logs vs telemetry metrics.
00:05:46 Priya: who has access to the logs on your side? we need RBAC and least-privilege.
00:05:52 Carlos: RBAC is role-based; internal SRE access is scoped to incident-driven sessions, with just-in-time access and audit trails. customers can request access logs for any session. Private gives you full control, Dedicated reduces cross-tenant access.
00:06:10 Owen: encryption in-flight? at-rest? we need end-to-end.
00:06:14 Carlos: TLS 1.2+ in-flight, at-rest AES-256, and envelope encryption with CMKs for keys. Private allows you to manage rotation cadence.

00:07:05 Leah: thanks, that's a good baseline. switching to a more operational scenario - suppose a regulator requests an export of all interactions for a EU user subset. what's the fastest path?
00:07:16 Carlos: if you're Private, you run the export internally; we provide tooling for manifest and signed digests. Dedicated requires a support-authored export with a signed request and we can pull manifests within 48 hours typically under our SLAs. Hosted depends on legal and support tier; we have an expedited process for enterprise customers.
00:07:44 Marta: 48 hours is ok for now, but if we need to do legal-hold longer we need immutable archives. can Redwood support WORM (write-once-read-many) archives?
00:07:54 Carlos: yes for Dedicated/Private we can configure immutable S3-style archives; hosted has add-ons to push to a tenant-managed archive for immutability.

00:08:30 Tommy: about telemetry sampling - our worry is that sampling could omit critical events during incidents. what's the default sampling and can it be turned off for our tenant?
00:08:39 Carlos: default sampling is on for Hosted to lower cost; Dedicated and Private can run full-fidelity capture. we can also configure burst-capture on incidents.

00:09:10 Owen: a slightly tricky ask - we sometimes need to scrub logs before handing to third parties. do you provide server-side redaction workflows or do we need to handle it before ingest?
00:09:19 Carlos: server-side redaction pipelines are available in Dedicated and Private; Hosted has pattern-based masking but not fully custom scrub pipelines. again, private gives you the most control.

00:09:45 Priya: regarding gdpr - data subject requests, right to be forgotten - can you guarantee deletion from backups? that's usually hard.
00:09:56 Leah: very common. for Private, you control backups. for Dedicated we'll work with you on backup retention policy and deletion windows and provide attestations. Hosted has reasonable deletion flows but long-term backups may require longer windows; we document the deletion SLA in the contract.

00:10:30 Marta: what's the cost delta? we need a rough sense of monthly per-100k requests for hosted vs dedicated vs private (amortized infra + licensing).
00:10:40 Leah: i'll get Carlos to do a conservative delta table — hosted is usually lowest TCO per-token but can spike with egress and long retention; dedicated adds base reserved cost but lowers per-token marginal costs and gives guaranteed qps; private has a higher fixed cost but is predictable for regulated workloads.
00:10:58 Carlos: we'll include both fixed + variable lines including snapshot and retention cost - and we'll show a break-even at roughly X requests (we'll compute with your numbers).

00:11:30 Marta: curious about fallbacks - if we put region-locking on hosted and a region outage happens, does traffic get sent to us or to another region? we need control over automatic failover.
00:11:42 Carlos: you can set a failover policy: fail open to a compatible model in another region (may need data residency waiver), fail to dedicated pool (if you have reserved capacity), or fail closed (reject). we can make those explicit in the rollout policy.

00:12:15 Owen: auditability — do you have runbooks for incident response and evidence packages?
00:12:21 Leah: yes we maintain incident runbooks and evidence packaging templates — we'll share the ops playbook example. it's fairly standard with manifest generation, signed hashes, and chain-of-custody notes.

00:13:00 Tommy: operational question - we run a private API gateway and can do mutual TLS. can we integrate Redwood Transparent Proxy or is there a supported integration?
00:13:10 Carlos: we have an edge connector that supports mTLS and private peering for Dedicated/Private. Hosted supports client certs but for full mTLS integration you want dedicated or private.

00:13:40 Marta: can we run smoke benchmarks? latency requirement is p95 under 250ms for short prompts in eu region.
00:13:51 Carlos: yes benching is standard — we'll do p95 latency numbers for your model/profile and for eu-west-1. for private/on-prem we need resource specs. I'll include a suggested hardware profile in the bench plan.

00:14:30 Priya: one more legal note — cross-border transfer implications for Ireland vs mainland EU, and potential subprocessor lists. can you provide a subprocessors list and where they operate?
00:14:43 Leah: yes — we have a subprocessors registry; i'll include the latest exports and map them by region.

00:15:10 Marta: are there any cases where Redwood stores request bodies long-term for model quality evals? we prefer an opt-in approach.
00:15:21 Carlos: default Hosted may retain anonymized samples by opt-out; for Dedicated/Private we can set opt-in and the default is no retention. we can also supply a data processing addendum to make this explicit.

00:15:48 Owen: hypotheticals - regulator wants raw transcripts, we want to supply sanitized manifests. how quickly can you produce binding attestations?
00:15:57 Leah: we can produce signed attestations and delivery manifests under enterprise contract; timing correlates with the evidence tier. typical target 72 business hours for large exports under dedicated/private but faster for scoped requests.

00:16:30 Marta: curious about key escrow again — if we lost keys, can Redwood help with recovery?
00:16:38 Carlos: key escrow is a special arrangement; we don't offer automatic escrow by default, but for private deployments you can integrate an HSM with shared escrow policies. we'll flag this as a legal thread.

00:17:05 Tommy: can you give an example of a recent bank customer who used dedicated to meet retention and residency? just high level.
00:17:12 Leah: yes - we supported a regional bank with dedicated pools in eu-west and private backups; they used dedicated for latency and compliance needs. i'll share a redacted case study.

00:17:35 Marta: last - we have ML teams that want to run small retraining/finetune with internal datasets. can Redwood support model ops in private?
00:17:46 Carlos: Private supports finetune pipelines and model hosting inside your network; dedicated can run closed-loop retrain jobs if containers are approved. we'll capture the scope in the technical deep dive.

00:18:20 Priya: ok. next steps recap?
00:18:23 Leah: recap - we'll send hosting matrix and subprocessors list, SOC2 artifacts, and bench plan. Carlos will schedule the technical deep dive and bench run. Ravenwood will share data flow and retention policy.
00:18:35 Marta: sounds good.
00:18:38 Tommy: thanks all.
00:18:41 Carlos: one more note — for the bench could you confirm target model behavior (generation vs embeddings) and token lengths? we'll need samples.
00:18:50 Marta: will do.

00:19:05 [crosstalk] Speaker 6: uh sorry joining late - is there a restriction on developer access to keys?
00:19:10 Carlos: you can restrict developer key creation via RBAC and require approval flows; we'll show policy examples.
00:19:22 Priya: please include a timeline for evidence export under a legal hold in the docs.
00:19:28 Leah: will add that to the follow up.

00:19:40 Meeting end - 19:48 UTC (note: call recorded).
